title: In 16 mice (Allen Neuropixels), omitted flashes gave no spike steps above a calibrated false-positive rate in 23 regions, and step share did not rise with connectome distance from the retina
abstract: Question: do brain regions far from the retina in the mesoscale connectome signal omitted expected stimuli more, and does a hippocampal omission signal exist at the first omissions a mouse ever sees? Data: Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels, 32 sessions from 16 mice (session 1 = first omission day, familiar images; session 2 = second day, novel images), active block, 21,921 QC unit entries in 23 regions, median 118 omissions per session. Method: a local discontinuity statistic at the expected flash time (linear trends cancel), one-sided Wilcoxon over omissions, and a shape calibration: the same test at times without an expected event gives each region's false-positive rate. Connectome distance from the retina (D_ret, Knox 2019) and 1,000 rewired maps came from sci:19f7eb8e. The plan was written before multi-session results and amended three times with stated reasons. Results: no time-locked omission step was found. The positive-step share was 3.2% at the expected time, 3.0-3.1% at +-50 ms and 1.8-1.9% at null locations; in session 1 every region group decreased smoothly across test locations with no peak at the expected time, and no region population step differed from zero. H1 failed: the excess share did not increase with D_ret (session 1 rho -0.21, mouse-bootstrap 95% CI -0.40 to 0.11; session 2 rho 0.02), while the flash-responsive share decreased with D_ret as expected (rho -0.39, CI -0.46 to -0.21). H2 failed: the hippocampal step at the first 20 omissions of session 1 was -0.17 Hz (16 mice, p = 0.95); the CA1 population step was -0.6% of baseline (CI -3.8% to +2.3%). Exploratory: in session 2, VISl and VISal had a local peak at the expected time (+3.5 percentage points, 10 of 16 mice, p = 0.11), which needs an independent test. An uncalibrated pre/post test flagged 10-16% of visual cortical units, so shape calibration is necessary. Limitations: unit tests detect only large steps (median 2.8 Hz); session also differs in image novelty; the passive block, running control and cell types were not tested; an average-mouse connectome model; 16 of 72 two-session mice. Code, aggregate tables, figures and byte-range provenance are included; Allen data stay external.

display.caption: Left and middle: percent of units with a positive step (p < 0.01) when the test is centred at different times c; a time-locked omission response would peak at c = 0. Bars: mouse-bootstrap 95% CI. Right: hippocampal mean step at the first 20 and last 40 omissions (mouse means).

Excess positive-step share against connectome distance from the retina (sessions 1 and 2, bars 95% CI), flash-responsive share against D_ret (positive control), and the rewired-connectome null for session 1.
Session 1 population PSTHs on omission and regular trials for five region groups. Lower row: units selected for a positive step (selection bias).

citations.reason: D_ret values and 1,000 rewired D_ret maps are used without change. Our flash-responsiveness control repeats its pattern: visual responses fall with D_ret, and rewired maps predict this equally well.
Its HTTP byte-range method for VBN unit spike times guided our fetcher, which is newly written.
Earlier structure-function work on the same VBN data set (engagement and wiring slope).
Prior VBN omission study. We agree that visual cortex has no time-locked omission response; with shape calibration we did not find hippocampal or MG step cells above the false-positive rate.
Knox et al. 2019 mesoscale connectome model behind D_ret.
